seo.meta_title: 눈치채다 Meaning | To Catch On in Korean, from A2O LITE's NEON
seo.meta_description: AI translates 눈치채다 as 'notice', but it means sensing something hidden — a secret, a mood, a plan. Plus 눈치 없다 and 눈치 보다.

ai_failure.situation: You're planning a surprise party and your Korean friend whispers 걔 눈치챘어? You ask AI what it means.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates it as 'Did she notice?', so you think it's about seeing something in plain view.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 눈치채다 means sensing something that hasn't been said: a secret, a plan, someone's real feelings. It comes from 눈치, the Korean skill of reading the room. The word appears in A2O LITE's 2026 debut song NEON.

natural_solution.rule: Use 눈치채다 for hidden things (secrets, feelings, plans). For something you simply see, use 알아차리다 or 보다.

alternatives.context: 'Did she catch on?' — about a surprise or a secret
'You're so clueless' — a common, mildly rude complaint among friends

alternatives.phrase: 상사 눈치 보느라 퇴근을 못 했어요.
alternatives.romanization: sang-sa nun-chi bo-neu-ra toe-geu-neul mot hae-sseo-yo
alternatives.context: 'I couldn't leave because I was watching my boss's mood'

nuance: 눈치 is one of the most important ideas in Korean social life: reading what others want without being told. 눈치 빠르다 (quick to read the room) is praise; 눈치 없다 is a criticism. See also 눈칫밥, eating while feeling unwelcome. 눈치채다 is written as one word.
